shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a calcified mass in the jaw with a chronic time course

shortlist.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the radiographic findings of a well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Possible explanation for the intraoral calcified mass and missing teeth

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Fits the description of a hard swelling over the right maxilla with an associated calcified lesion

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common, cherubism can present with bilateral jaw lesions, but the unilateral presentation in this case is still plausible

raw.rationale: The presence of a calcified mass in the right maxillary molar area, missing teeth, and an extensive, well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion in the right maxilla are consistent with a complex odontoma, which is a type of benign odontogenic tumor that can cause swelling and tooth displacement.

rejected.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and may have a softer consistency than the hard swelling described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor often presents as a well-circumscribed radiolucency with a characteristic 'egg-shell' rim of calcification, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: This tumor typically presents as a well-defined radiopacity, but it may not be as extensively calcified as the lesion described in the vignette, and it often has a softer consistency.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with bilateral involvement of the mandible and maxilla, and it often has a familial component, which is not mentioned in the vignette.
